newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan should intervene to push up yen-Bergsten.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan should intervene to push up yen-Bergsten.

text.p: The United States and Japan should become much more explicit about their desire for a stronger yen and intervene in the currency markets to bring that about, economist Fred Bergsten said on Wednesday.
"Intervention could be very helpful," said Bergsten, a former U.S. official who now heads the Institute for International Economics think tank here.

Speaking to reporters after a news conference called by exporters who oppose unilateral U.S. trade sanctions, Bergsten said the intervention should be timed to hit the market when the yen is starting to retrace some of its recent fall.

The intervention would be even more effective if it was accompanied by changes in Japanese economic policy, including a shift by Tokyo away from its planned stringent budget stance, he said. But it should go ahead nonetheless.
"If the yen remains at anything like current levels, there will be a huge renewed surge in the Japanese (trade) surplus that will take it to all-time record levels," Bergsten said.

While short-run economic fundamentals favor the dollar -- U.S. interest rates are rising and the U.S. economy is strong -- the longer-run fundamentals argue for a stronger yen, in the range of 100 to 110 to the dollar, he added.
